pointers.sentence: The built-in filters are the functions of `django/template/defaultfilters.py`, from `|upper` and `|date` to `|default` and `|length`, which every template has without `{% load %}`.

The parser finds a filter by name when it compiles `{{ ship.name|upper }}`, and checks its arguments ([Variables and filters: `FilterExpression` and `Variable`](variables.md)); at render time `FilterExpression.resolve` passes the value through each filter in turn (`django/template/base.py:FilterExpression.resolve`).

`django/template/defaultfilters.py` makes one `Library`, `register`, and decorates each filter with `Library.filter`, which stores it under its own name or the one given, as `escape_filter` is stored as `|escape`, and sets the flags it is given as attributes on it and, for a decorator such as `stringfilter` to read, on the innermost function under it (`django/template/library.py:Library.filter`).

`django/template/defaultfilters.py` makes one `Library`, `register`, and decorates each filter with `Library.filter`, which stores it under its own name or the one given, as `escape_filter` is stored as `|escape`, and sets the flags it is given as attributes on it and, for a decorator such as `stringfilter` to read, on the innermost function under it (`django/template/library.py:Library.filter`).

Most string filters also wear `stringfilter`, which calls `str` on the first argument, so that `|lower` works on a number's text, and marks the result safe when that argument was a `SafeData` and the function has `is_safe=True` (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:stringfilter`).
`|upper`, `|urlencode` and `|wordcount` carry `is_safe=False`, and `|cut` no flag: it keeps its input's safety unless the text removed was `";"` (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:cut`).

When it is on, each escapes what of its input is not safe, adds its markup, numbers or separator and returns the whole through `mark_safe`; called from Python, they escape by default (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:linebreaksbr`).

`|urlize` and `|urlizetrunc` call `django.utils.html.urlize` with `nofollow=True`, which splits the text at white space, quotes and angle brackets, trims each word's wrapping and trailing punctuation, and links what is left if it is an `"http"` or `"https"` URL, a name beginning `"www."` or ending in one of the seven original top-level domains, or an email address, given `"mailto:"` and no `rel="nofollow"` (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer`).
`floatformat` reads the value as a `decimal.Decimal`, through `str` or else `float`, and gives `""` for what is not a number (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:floatformat`).
`dictsort` and `dictsortreversed` sort by a key that `_property_resolver` makes (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:_property_resolver`).
`length` is `len`, or `0` (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:length`).

`|length` calls `QuerySet.__len__`, which fills the result cache, so a `{% for %}` over the same `QuerySet` sends no second query; a variable that ends in a method, as `{{ port.ship_set.all }}` does, gives a new `QuerySet`, and a new query, each time it is resolved (`django/template/base.py:Variable._resolve_lookup`).
`|last` asks for index -1, which `QuerySet.__getitem__` refuses with `ValueError`, and as `last` catches only `IndexError`, the render fails (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.__getitem__`).
`date` and `time` format with the letters of PHP's date function (`django/utils/dateformat.py`).

Their `expects_localtime=True` has `FilterExpression.resolve` first convert an aware datetime to the current time zone, unless `Context.use_tz`, or `USE_TZ` when that is unset, is false, as inside `{% localtime off %}`, or a filter of `{% load tz %}` such as `|utc` has converted it already (`django/utils/timezone.py:template_localtime`, `django/templatetags/tz.py:do_timezone`).

Their `expects_localtime=True` has `FilterExpression.resolve` first convert an aware datetime to the current time zone, unless `Context.use_tz`, or `USE_TZ` when that is unset, is false, as inside `{% localtime off %}`, or a filter of `{% load tz %}` such as `|utc` has converted it already (`django/utils/timezone.py:template_localtime`, `django/templatetags/tz.py:do_timezone`).

`date` passes its argument to `django.utils.formats.date_format`, which looks it up as a format's name, in the active language's format modules and then the format settings, and takes an argument that names none as the format itself (`django/utils/formats.py:get_format`).

Both give `""` for `None`, `""` or a value without the parts its letters ask for; but a `datetime.date` asked for a time letter, as by `|date:"H:i"`, raises `TypeError`, which `date` does not catch, and the render fails (`django/utils/dateformat.py:Formatter.format`).
`|timesince` and `|timeuntil` put the time between the value and the argument, or now, into words (`django/utils/timesince.py:timesince`).
`default` returns `value or arg`, replacing any false value; `default_if_none` replaces only `None` (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:default`).
With it set, the string is returned at once and no filter runs (`django/template/base.py:FilterExpression.resolve`).
`pluralize` takes a plural suffix, `"s"` by default, or a singular and a plural, `"y,ies"` (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:pluralize`).

`|divisibleby` tells whether `int` of the value divides by `int` of the argument, and a value that is not a number ends the render (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:yesno`, `django/template/defaultfilters.py:divisibleby`).
